text: dsh-open-bots 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的个性化 bots 插件，会在 Harness 中挂载 Host 模块，并通过 Bots 面板管理长期存在的多个 bot。用户可以为 bot 设置身份与专属模型，在 bot 会话中使用记忆读写和 bot 间消息工具；界面展示 bot 列表、状态及设置。插件还包含可选的语音相关模块。适合希望在 DSH 中创建多个具有不同身份、记忆和模型配置的助手的用户。语音能力需要配置相应语音服务的密钥。

dsh-open-bots creates persistent bots for DSH Web. Its Bots panel shows bot lists, status, and settings. Users can set each bot’s identity and model, use memory tools, and send messages between bots. Optional voice features use a selected speech provider and its API key.
想在 DSH 里创建几个身份和模型各不相同的长期助手
我想让不同的 bot 各自记住相关资料，并在后续对话中调用
I want a DSH panel where I can manage several persistent bots and their settings.
dsh-open-bots 的功能「Bots 管理面板」：在 DSH 侧栏提供 Bots 页面，展示 bot 列表、状态与设置，并支持创建 bot、更新身份和选择模型。
dsh-open-bots 的功能「分 bot 记忆」：bot 可保存并检索 bot 自身或用户范围的资料；系统会按对话内容自动挑选相关事实作为后续对话上下文。
dsh-open-bots 使用前须知：启用语音能力时，语音请求会发送给所选服务商，例如 ElevenLabs；对应服务需配置自己的 API 密钥。（见 src/host/voice-providers.js:43-56）

dsh-open-bots README · dsh-open-bots：Lasting bots for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Each bot
outlives the conversation and has its own name, photo, persona, memory, voice and model. You
configure it by talking to it ("from now on your name is Ana", "be more direct", "use this
photo"), and it runs on any model in your Harness catalog, open-weight models included. Behind
each bot, a hidden **brain** follows the conversation and prepares what will help: it looks things
up before you ask, and, when the bot plays a guiding role (therapist, teacher, coach), it leaves the
bot techniques of that craft to apply in its own words.

dsh-open-bots README · dsh-open-bots：> **Status: 0.1.0, the first public release.** Tested on DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.3, Desktop
> and `dsh web`, on Windows. macOS is expected to work (no native modules, no shell commands) but
> was not tested. See [Compatibility](#compatibility) and [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).
>
> **Language:** the interface and the text the bots receive (persona rules, the brain's
> instructions, tool messages) are in Brazilian Portuguese for now, and the bots are tuned for
> conversations in Portuguese. The code, docs and comments are in English.

dsh-open-bots README · What it does：- **A leader bot from the first start.** It, and any other bot, creates new bots when you ask.
- **Identity by conversation.** Ask a bot to change its name, title, persona, method, photo,
  model or voice, and it changes on the spot. Every change can be undone.
- **Memory in two layers:**
  - the persona, always present in the conversation;
  - the facts, saved one by one by topic: a small memory goes into each turn whole, a larger one
    is searched automatically on each message.

dsh-open-bots README · What it does：Each bot has its own memory, plus a memory about you that every bot reads.
- **A light, live panel.** A **Bots** panel in the sidebar shows each bot's photo, name and live
  state, with its settings (photo, model, permission, voice, leader, delete). "New conversation"
  is always in sight on each bot and at the top of its conversation. The panel opens at once with
  the last saved list and updates by itself.
- **Permissions under your control.** A bot follows the access you chose for new conversations,
  and you can narrow it. To go past it, the bot asks for your "yes" on screen.
- **Bots talking to bots.** A bot asks another one and gets the answer in the same turn.
- **Errors explained by the bot.** When a model fails (quota, missing key, unknown model), the bot
  explains it to you in plain words in its next answer, and the panel shows a discreet mark.

dsh-open-bots README · The brain：Each bot has a brain: a hidden subagent that follows the conversation without ever talking to the
person. What it finds reaches the bot as notes on a **board** that the bot reads before each
answer, and the bot uses them as things it already knows.

dsh-open-bots README · The brain：- **Looks ahead.** Tell the bot about a trip and the brain looks up the weather and things to do;
  hesitate between two products and it looks up prices and specs.
- **Guides by craft.** When the bot plays a guiding role (therapist, teacher, coach, mentor), the
  brain leaves the technique of that craft for the moment, as an intent ("ask for the concrete
  scene, let the person choose where to start"), never as a ready-made line. The bot applies it in
  its own words and never mentions the brain.
- **Tasks on request.** When something needs current data, the bot hands it to the brain as a
  task, says it will look, and tells the person when the result arrives.
- **Cheap when idle.** A quick question to the model decides whether an exchange needs any work
  at all. Only then does the brain start, and it stays for the rest of the conversation, receiving
  each new exchange instead of a new brain being started every time (renewed after 30 exchanges or
  20 minutes without one).
- **Nothing to configure.** The brain uses the bot's own model. To change it, ask the bot ("use
  the Nemotron for your brain"); it applies to the brain's next piece of work.

dsh-open-bots README · The brain：The design is in [docs/brain.md](docs/brain.md).

dsh-open-bots README · Voice：Voice works with the speech service you already use. The plugin recognizes the service from the
key: **ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Groq, Mistral or Deepgram**, or your own server in the OpenAI format.

dsh-open-bots README · Voice：- **Dictation in your language** through the Harness's official microphone ("Voice input").
- **Each bot with its own voice.** A **Listen** button on each answer reads it in the bot's voice.
  Voice and speed live in the bot's settings, with a sample, or the bot changes them when you ask.
  With ElevenLabs you can search its voice library in the bot's language, or create a voice from
  a description: the bot makes 3 previews, you listen and choose. Nothing is created or added
  unless you ask.
- **Live voice conversation.** In a bot's conversation, the **Voz** tab turns into a face-to-face
  call: the bot's photo, a ring that shows who is speaking, the microphone open and the answer
  spoken while the bot writes. Talk over it to interrupt; everything stays written in the
  conversation. Needs a service with live listening and speech (today, ElevenLabs).
dsh-open-bots README · Voice：The design is in [docs/voice-mode.md](docs/voice-mode.md).

dsh-open-bots README · Responsible use：- **A bot is not a professional.** Bots can take on roles like therapist or coach, and the brain
  helps them guide a conversation, but they are language models: they make mistakes, and they are
  not a substitute for a licensed professional. Do not rely on them in a crisis; look for local
  emergency services or a crisis line.
- **You choose the models.** The plugin adds no content filter of its own; what a bot says depends
  on the model and the persona you give it.
- **Your conversations stay where your Harness runs,** except what goes to the model provider and
  the voice service you configured (see [Where your data lives](#where-your-data-lives)).

dsh-open-bots README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0` (Desktop or `dsh web`).
- At least one chat model configured in the Harness. The brain's web search uses the Harness's
  web search tool.
- For voice (optional): a key for one of the services above, or your own server.

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：For people and for AI agents. Each step says what you should see; stop at the first step that
does not match.

**AI agents:** never ask for a key in the chat, and never write one to a file yourself. Keys are
the user's step ([Credentials](#credentials)).

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：1. **Get the package.** Download `dsh-open-bots-<version>.tgz` from the
   [latest release](https://github.com/dev-bravelo/dsh-open-bots/releases), or build it from the
   source (needs Node.js 20.6 or later and Git):
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/dev-bravelo/dsh-open-bots.git
   cd dsh-open-bots
   npm pack
   ```
   You should have a file `dsh-open-bots-<version>.tgz`. There are no dependencies to install.

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：2. **Install it in your Harness profile.** Either:
   - in a Harness session, ask the agent to install the bundle from that file with the plugin
     manager (`plugin_manager` → `install_bundle`, with the absolute path of the `.tgz`); or
   - close the Harness and run its command line, then open the Harness again:
     ```bash
     dsh plugin --profile desktop add "file:<absolute path>/dsh-open-bots-<version>.tgz"
     ```
     The Desktop app uses the profile `desktop`.

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：You should see `dsh-open-bots` listed as installed and enabled.
   - **Stop if** it is listed as `incompatible-version`: your Harness is outside the supported
     range.

3. **Open the Bots panel** in the sidebar. You should see the leader bot. Open its conversation
   and say hello; ask it to create another bot ("create a bot called Nina, a cheerful English
   teacher").

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：4. **Optional: voice.** Turn on **Voice input** in the Harness's Plugins panel. In the
   **dsh-open-bots voice** section (in the details of Voice input, or on the plugin's page), paste
   the key of your speech service. The plugin recognizes the service, tests the key there, stores
   it in the Harness credential vault and starts using it.

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：**To remove it:** uninstall the bundle with the plugin manager. Your bots' files stay in the data folder until you delete them
([Where your data lives](#where-your-data-lives)).

dsh-open-bots README · Configuration：Everything works without configuration. Optional settings go in your profile's patch file,
`<Harness home>/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` (a YAML list; add the entry to it):

```yaml
- id: open-bots
  name: dsh-open-bots
  config:
    voice:

`<Harness home>` is `~/.dsh`, or `$DSH_HOME` when set. A bot's own brain model, chosen by talking
to it, wins over `cerebro`. `home` sets another data folder (default `<Harness home>/open-bots`).

dsh-open-bots README · Credentials：Keys are referenced by name and read from the Harness credential vault when needed: never stored
in the plugin's files, never sent to the interface, never asked for in a chat.

| Service | Key name |
|---|---|
| ElevenLabs | `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` |
| OpenAI | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| Groq | `GROQ_API_KEY` |
| Mistral | `MISTRAL_API_KEY` |
| Deepgram | `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` |

dsh-open-bots README · Credentials：Paste a key in the **dsh-open-bots voice** section, or put it in the vault yourself, in
`<Harness home>/.credentials.yaml` under `refs:`, or as an environment variable. For live voice,
the interface gets single-use tokens that the host part creates from the key (valid for 15
minutes, one per connection); the key itself never reaches the interface.

dsh-open-bots README · Where your data lives：Everything stays in `<Harness home>/open-bots/` on the machine where the Harness runs:

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `bots/<id>/persona.md` | the bot's persona |
| `bots/<id>/registro/` | the bot's facts, one file per topic |
| `usuario/persona.md`, `usuario/registro/` | what every bot knows about you |
| `bots/<id>/historico.jsonl` | identity changes, so they can be undone |
| `bots/<id>/fotos/` | the bot's photo, with earlier ones kept for undo |

dsh-open-bots README · Where your data lives：The brain's board lives in memory, for the current conversation only. The conversations
themselves are ordinary Harness sessions. What leaves your machine: the requests to the model
provider of each bot and of its brain, the brain's web searches through the Harness, and audio and
text to the voice service you configured.

dsh-open-bots README · Compatibility：- **DeepSeek Harness:** `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0` (`engines.dsh`). Tested on 0.2.1-rc.3, Desktop
  and `dsh web`, on Windows.
- **Official APIs only:** the plugin does not patch the Harness application.
- **When the Harness updates:** each module is a sub-plugin with its own dependencies, and what is
  not a public contract sits in a small adapter with its own test, so an update breaks a test, not
  your bots.
- **Known limit:** the resident brain stays open while it waits for the next exchange. Hosts that
  wait for every subagent of a conversation to finish (headless runs, goals, the SDK `wait`, ACP)
  would wait for it until it is renewed (up to 20 minutes). Bot conversations are meant for the
  Desktop and `dsh web`.

dsh-open-bots README · Development：| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run hooks` | Points git to `.githooks/` (run once per clone) |
| `npm run test:harness` | Installs the published Harness in `dev/harness/<version>` (outside Git), once, and runs the tests against it |
| `npm test` | Unit tests, against the Harness installed by `npm run test:harness` |
| `npm run check` | Secret and personal-data scan, then the tests |
| `node scripts/ensaio.mjs` | Starts a test Harness (`dsh web`) in a separate folder with this package installed, without touching your own profile. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` for the model route and keys |

dsh-open-bots README · Development：Contributor and AI-agent rules are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md); the architecture is in
[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

dsh-open-bots README · Credits：DS Bot (Apache-2.0) was a reference for building lasting bots on the Harness. This project is
independent.

dsh-open-bots README · dsh-open-bots：Lasting bots for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Each bot
outlives the conversation and has its own name, photo, persona, memory, voice and model. You
configure it by talking to it ("from now on your name is Ana", "be more direct", "use this
photo"), and it runs on any model in your Harness catalog, open-weight models included. Behind
each bot, a hidden **brain** follows the conversation and prepares what will help: it looks things
up before you ask, and, when the bot plays a guiding role (therapist, teacher, coach), it leaves the
bot techniques of that craft to apply in its own words.

dsh-open-bots README · dsh-open-bots：> **Status: 0.1.0, the first public release.** Tested on DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.3, Desktop
> and `dsh web`, on Windows. macOS is expected to work (no native modules, no shell commands) but
> was not tested. See [Compatibility](#compatibility) and [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).
>
> **Language:** the interface and the text the bots receive (persona rules, the brain's
> instructions, tool messages) are in Brazilian Portuguese for now, and the bots are tuned for
> conversations in Portuguese. The code, docs and comments are in English.

dsh-open-bots README · What it does：- **A leader bot from the first start.** It, and any other bot, creates new bots when you ask.
- **Identity by conversation.** Ask a bot to change its name, title, persona, method, photo,
  model or voice, and it changes on the spot. Every change can be undone.
- **Memory in two layers:**
  - the persona, always present in the conversation;
  - the facts, saved one by one by topic: a small memory goes into each turn whole, a larger one
    is searched automatically on each message.

dsh-open-bots README · What it does：Each bot has its own memory, plus a memory about you that every bot reads.
- **A light, live panel.** A **Bots** panel in the sidebar shows each bot's photo, name and live
  state, with its settings (photo, model, permission, voice, leader, delete). "New conversation"
  is always in sight on each bot and at the top of its conversation. The panel opens at once with
  the last saved list and updates by itself.
- **Permissions under your control.** A bot follows the access you chose for new conversations,
  and you can narrow it. To go past it, the bot asks for your "yes" on screen.
- **Bots talking to bots.** A bot asks another one and gets the answer in the same turn.
- **Errors explained by the bot.** When a model fails (quota, missing key, unknown model), the bot
  explains it to you in plain words in its next answer, and the panel shows a discreet mark.

dsh-open-bots README · The brain：Each bot has a brain: a hidden subagent that follows the conversation without ever talking to the
person. What it finds reaches the bot as notes on a **board** that the bot reads before each
answer, and the bot uses them as things it already knows.

dsh-open-bots README · The brain：- **Looks ahead.** Tell the bot about a trip and the brain looks up the weather and things to do;
  hesitate between two products and it looks up prices and specs.
- **Guides by craft.** When the bot plays a guiding role (therapist, teacher, coach, mentor), the
  brain leaves the technique of that craft for the moment, as an intent ("ask for the concrete
  scene, let the person choose where to start"), never as a ready-made line. The bot applies it in
  its own words and never mentions the brain.
- **Tasks on request.** When something needs current data, the bot hands it to the brain as a
  task, says it will look, and tells the person when the result arrives.
- **Cheap when idle.** A quick question to the model decides whether an exchange needs any work
  at all. Only then does the brain start, and it stays for the rest of the conversation, receiving
  each new exchange instead of a new brain being started every time (renewed after 30 exchanges or
  20 minutes without one).
- **Nothing to configure.** The brain uses the bot's own model. To change it, ask the bot ("use
  the Nemotron for your brain"); it applies to the brain's next piece of work.

dsh-open-bots README · The brain：The design is in [docs/brain.md](docs/brain.md).

dsh-open-bots README · Voice：Voice works with the speech service you already use. The plugin recognizes the service from the
key: **ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Groq, Mistral or Deepgram**, or your own server in the OpenAI format.

dsh-open-bots README · Voice：- **Dictation in your language** through the Harness's official microphone ("Voice input").
- **Each bot with its own voice.** A **Listen** button on each answer reads it in the bot's voice.
  Voice and speed live in the bot's settings, with a sample, or the bot changes them when you ask.
  With ElevenLabs you can search its voice library in the bot's language, or create a voice from
  a description: the bot makes 3 previews, you listen and choose. Nothing is created or added
  unless you ask.
- **Live voice conversation.** In a bot's conversation, the **Voz** tab turns into a face-to-face
  call: the bot's photo, a ring that shows who is speaking, the microphone open and the answer
  spoken while the bot writes. Talk over it to interrupt; everything stays written in the
  conversation. Needs a service with live listening and speech (today, ElevenLabs).
dsh-open-bots README · Voice：The design is in [docs/voice-mode.md](docs/voice-mode.md).

dsh-open-bots README · Responsible use：- **A bot is not a professional.** Bots can take on roles like therapist or coach, and the brain
  helps them guide a conversation, but they are language models: they make mistakes, and they are
  not a substitute for a licensed professional. Do not rely on them in a crisis; look for local
  emergency services or a crisis line.
- **You choose the models.** The plugin adds no content filter of its own; what a bot says depends
  on the model and the persona you give it.
- **Your conversations stay where your Harness runs,** except what goes to the model provider and
  the voice service you configured (see [Where your data lives](#where-your-data-lives)).

dsh-open-bots README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0` (Desktop or `dsh web`).
- At least one chat model configured in the Harness. The brain's web search uses the Harness's
  web search tool.
- For voice (optional): a key for one of the services above, or your own server.

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：For people and for AI agents. Each step says what you should see; stop at the first step that
does not match.

**AI agents:** never ask for a key in the chat, and never write one to a file yourself. Keys are
the user's step ([Credentials](#credentials)).

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：1. **Get the package.** Download `dsh-open-bots-<version>.tgz` from the
   [latest release](https://github.com/dev-bravelo/dsh-open-bots/releases), or build it from the
   source (needs Node.js 20.6 or later and Git):
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/dev-bravelo/dsh-open-bots.git
   cd dsh-open-bots
   npm pack
   ```
   You should have a file `dsh-open-bots-<version>.tgz`. There are no dependencies to install.

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：2. **Install it in your Harness profile.** Either:
   - in a Harness session, ask the agent to install the bundle from that file with the plugin
     manager (`plugin_manager` → `install_bundle`, with the absolute path of the `.tgz`); or
   - close the Harness and run its command line, then open the Harness again:
     ```bash
     dsh plugin --profile desktop add "file:<absolute path>/dsh-open-bots-<version>.tgz"
     ```
     The Desktop app uses the profile `desktop`.

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：You should see `dsh-open-bots` listed as installed and enabled.
   - **Stop if** it is listed as `incompatible-version`: your Harness is outside the supported
     range.

3. **Open the Bots panel** in the sidebar. You should see the leader bot. Open its conversation
   and say hello; ask it to create another bot ("create a bot called Nina, a cheerful English
   teacher").

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：4. **Optional: voice.** Turn on **Voice input** in the Harness's Plugins panel. In the
   **dsh-open-bots voice** section (in the details of Voice input, or on the plugin's page), paste
   the key of your speech service. The plugin recognizes the service, tests the key there, stores
   it in the Harness credential vault and starts using it.

dsh-open-bots README · Installation：**To remove it:** uninstall the bundle with the plugin manager. Your bots' files stay in the data folder until you delete them
([Where your data lives](#where-your-data-lives)).

dsh-open-bots README · Configuration：Everything works without configuration. Optional settings go in your profile's patch file,
`<Harness home>/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` (a YAML list; add the entry to it):

```yaml
- id: open-bots
  name: dsh-open-bots
  config:
    voice:

`<Harness home>` is `~/.dsh`, or `$DSH_HOME` when set. A bot's own brain model, chosen by talking
to it, wins over `cerebro`. `home` sets another data folder (default `<Harness home>/open-bots`).

dsh-open-bots README · Credentials：Keys are referenced by name and read from the Harness credential vault when needed: never stored
in the plugin's files, never sent to the interface, never asked for in a chat.

| Service | Key name |
|---|---|
| ElevenLabs | `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` |
| OpenAI | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| Groq | `GROQ_API_KEY` |
| Mistral | `MISTRAL_API_KEY` |
| Deepgram | `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` |

dsh-open-bots README · Credentials：Paste a key in the **dsh-open-bots voice** section, or put it in the vault yourself, in
`<Harness home>/.credentials.yaml` under `refs:`, or as an environment variable. For live voice,
the interface gets single-use tokens that the host part creates from the key (valid for 15
minutes, one per connection); the key itself never reaches the interface.

dsh-open-bots README · Where your data lives：Everything stays in `<Harness home>/open-bots/` on the machine where the Harness runs:

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `bots/<id>/persona.md` | the bot's persona |
| `bots/<id>/registro/` | the bot's facts, one file per topic |
| `usuario/persona.md`, `usuario/registro/` | what every bot knows about you |
| `bots/<id>/historico.jsonl` | identity changes, so they can be undone |
| `bots/<id>/fotos/` | the bot's photo, with earlier ones kept for undo |

dsh-open-bots README · Where your data lives：The brain's board lives in memory, for the current conversation only. The conversations
themselves are ordinary Harness sessions. What leaves your machine: the requests to the model
provider of each bot and of its brain, the brain's web searches through the Harness, and audio and
text to the voice service you configured.

dsh-open-bots README · Compatibility：- **DeepSeek Harness:** `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0` (`engines.dsh`). Tested on 0.2.1-rc.3, Desktop
  and `dsh web`, on Windows.
- **Official APIs only:** the plugin does not patch the Harness application.
- **When the Harness updates:** each module is a sub-plugin with its own dependencies, and what is
  not a public contract sits in a small adapter with its own test, so an update breaks a test, not
  your bots.
- **Known limit:** the resident brain stays open while it waits for the next exchange. Hosts that
  wait for every subagent of a conversation to finish (headless runs, goals, the SDK `wait`, ACP)
  would wait for it until it is renewed (up to 20 minutes). Bot conversations are meant for the
  Desktop and `dsh web`.
